name: AD — SPN Added by Non-Computer Principal (Kerberoast Setup)
description:
Attacker objective
Set a Service Principal Name on an account (especially a user account) to make it Kerberoastable.

Attack logic
Computer accounts self-register SPNs and are excluded. A human or service principal adding an SPN — particularly to a user account — is a Kerberoast-setup pattern that precedes an RC4/service-ticket request.

Why this detection works
Event 5136 records servicePrincipalName additions with the acting subject, so excluding computer principals isolates the setup behaviour.

False positives
Administrative service-account provisioning.

Tuning
Allowlist provisioning admins; an SPN added to a user account is highest-risk.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 5136 (AttributeLDAPDisplayName=servicePrincipalName, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SubjectUserName added the SPN; ObjectDN = the account.
2. If the target is a user account, rotate its password and watch for a subsequent RC4 service-ticket request.
query: event.code:"5136" and winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName:"servicePrincipalName" and not winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName:*$ and not winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName:"SYSTEM"
